Commentary.Commentary: ...Second innings...

The debutant, Nahid Rana was having an off day. Sri Lanka deliberately took him on and scored a lot of him but the debutant wasn't going to let it slip away that easily as Rana made a fine comeback by picking both set batters. He ended with three wickets and so did Khaled Ahmed. The pitch might do a bit with the new ball. Bangladesh have to be aware of that. They will hope to end the day's play without losing any wickets. Can the openers lay the foundation?

Sri Lanka end with a decent total. Bangladesh will be happy with how they have fought back. It was just the second session that has let them down. Five wickets in first session and five in this one but Sri Lanka turned things around in the second session when Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis came into bat under tremendous pressure. A partnership was badly needed and both played such wonderfully that it hushed Bangladesh completely on the back foot. Sri Lanka scored around 5 runs per over and both added around 200 runs. Both fell right after getting to their respective tons.

Dhananjaya De Silva and Mendis have turned things around and did in some fashion. Right from the start of this session, they put Bangladesh under pressure by scoring boundaries regularly. Bangladesh looked very loose in this session, completely different from what we saw early on but if it continues the same way, Dhananjaya De Silva and Mendis won't mind at all. Bangladesh need to reshuffle and get things back in order to break this stubborn partnership. Stay tuned for the final session.

LUNCH BREAK! A commanding start by the hosts! Overcast conditions, ball moving both ways and the seamers right on the money, Bangladesh couldn't have asked for a better start than this! They made the most of the pitch by bowling in tight lines and lengths. Khaled Ahmed was the pick of the lot. He was just brilliant. Got Nishan Madushka at the start and Dimuth Karunaratne and Kusal Mendis in one over. Angelo Mathews was run out. Dinesh Chandimal was trapped on the leg side. Kamindu Mendis too nicked his first ball but was dropped at slips. Now, Dhananjaya De Silva and Mendis have started to rebuild. The pair have looked in fine rhythm. Sri Lanka though will hope they put on a big stand but Bangladesh have their tails up and they will be rearing to go in the next session. Stay tuned.
